chapter: Art Hodes, Bechet and Blue Note
title: Alfred Lion and the Blue Note studios
summary: Lion and Francis Wolff were nice to him; Moore remembers the office and where they recorded.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Alfred Lion as a producer, what did you think of him?
He was a nice fellow. There were two fellows together.
Yeah. I think one of them passed away.
We're talking about Blue Note Records. Of course, you... Where were their studios, as a matter of fact, for Blue Note? Where were the Blue Note studios? Do you remember?

Let's see, I don't know if it was a studio or not... I think they had a place at 61st Street and Fifth Avenue. That's where they had all the records. They used to give the records... I used to go down and they'd give me as many records as I want -- give them to me, you know.
Where did you record for them?

It was never the same place... I think down on 47th Street, somewhere down in there... 48th Street and Eighth Avenue...? I know the...I don't know if it was a studio or what it was. But it was at 61st Street and Fifth Avenue, I think it was the third floor...
61st and Eighth Avenue, that would put us right in the vicinity of...
Well, there isn't a 61st and Fifth. You'd be right in Central Park. [ACTUALLY, IT COULD HAVE BEEN ON 61st BETWEEN FIFTH AND MADISON]
